parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence; sodomy repealed (1988); functioning courts repeatedly rule for LGBT people; documented social acceptance (large Prides, majority marriage support). But the traveller-facing record shows an unremedied universal exposure: the main airport has no trans-interaction regulations, with documented humiliating questioning, detainment and surgery demanded during gender screening (2023). Anti-LGBT violence rose to a record 433 physical incidents in 2025, trans people bearing the brunt, with organised dating-app ambushes. If detained, custody practice is segregation by birth sex, with trans women held in men's prisons; judicial relief exists case-by-case but its reach to a foreign visitor is unestablished. Protections are strong; the border gap and rising patterned violence hold the score at the band boundary.

entry_documents.exposure: Main international airport has no regulations for interacting with trans travellers; May 2023 first-person account documents humiliating gender-identity screening, detainment, and staff insisting 'if you don't undergo surgery, you're still a male.' Dossier states border screening can out a traveller.
entry_documents.protection: No documented entry bar or marker-based refusal; legal gender change without surgery (2015) and dead-name removal (2024) exist as climate signals; 2025 court upheld an existing gender-change certificate.
entry_documents.interaction: Screening at entry feeds directly into detention and, if charges follow, birth-sex/segregation custody; document-presentation mismatch is the gateway exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Airport detainment documented (2023). Custody practice isolates and segregates trans prisoners rather than housing by gender identity (2015 law journal); trans women have been held in men's prisons. No statute or prison-service regulation on placement is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: October 2019 court ordered HRT and transfer of a trans woman from a men's prison to a women's prison after NGO petition; 2023 police regulation governs searches of transgender people after complaints about humiliating searches.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Case-by-case judicial relief may not extend to a detained foreign visitor; segregation default would govern a visitor's placement if arrested.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National law is uniform; no subnational facility or custody divergence documented. Municipal posture varies (Pride bans, flag-raising) but no city is shown safer or less safe.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Court overturned a municipal Pride ban; municipalities host Prides, an LGBT community centre, and recognise same-sex partners as family units.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Municipal tolerance does not modify national border screening or prison placement rules.

care_services.exposure: Single approval Committee for Sex Reassignment gates publicly funded transition care with stringent criteria; residents pay out of pocket or travel abroad. Whether emergency care for an outed visitor is affected is not documented.
care_services.protection: Public insurance covers approved treatment; conversion therapy banned for licensed professionals by 2022 health-minister directive (clergy/alternative practitioners not bound).
care_services.interaction: Visitor uses home-country prescriptions; no documented customs or refill seizure issue.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State is not the perpetrator: no trans-specific criminal offence, no documented police targeting. But airport security framed the traveller as still male absent surgery — institutional threat-framing at the border.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-crime status doubles punishment for orientation-motivated violence; employment (1992), defamation (1997) and services (2000) anti-discrimination statutes; courts enforce repeatedly.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Whether gender identity, distinct from orientation, is a named protected ground in these statutes is unresolved in the sources.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented traveller-specific rules for a minor. Rising anti-LGBT violence and organised ambushes would apply equally to an outed accompanying minor; conversion therapy by clergy or alternative practitioners remains unregulated.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion therapy banned for licensed professionals; no documented minor-targeted hostility or age-differentiated penalty.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented whether an unaccompanied or accompanied minor faces different border screening.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2025 official data: 433 homophobic/transphobic physical incidents, rising to a record, trans people 'bearing the brunt'; dating-app traps and organised ambushes luring victims to attacks. Lethal violence at public expression: 2009 centre shooting (2 killed), 2015 pride attack killing a teenager. Feb 2025 foreign anti-trans rhetoric inflaming local climate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Perpetrators prosecuted: 10-year sentence for 2005 attack, sentence after 2015 killing; pride ban overturned by court; Tolerance Square memorial; hundreds of thousands march at Pride.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Record-high raw counts lack a population denominator, so per-capita rate versus other jurisdictions is not established; patterned and rising nonetheless.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented remedy for airport gender screening; no prison-placement statute; whether case-by-case judicial relief reaches a detained foreign visitor is unestablished; whether gender identity is a named protected statutory ground is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts demonstrably function for LGBT people (pride ban, HRT/transfer, surrogacy equality, deportation protection, 2025 certificate ruling); hate-crime sentencing; 2023 police search regulation; active NGO litigation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working courts mitigate street and custody harm but have not been shown to correct the border practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than Vellandra: no entry bar, Visitor Conduct Register, airline registration or near-total exclusion; no effective-remedy failure at admission. Our exposure is humiliating screening and occasional detainment, not designed refusal of entry.

Similar in border mechanics: extended secondary screening, humiliation, refused admission possible, slow remedies. Ours adds far stronger statutory/court protections and documented public acceptance, but adds patterned rising street violence and birth-sex custody practice if detained.

Higher than Vellmaris on the same axis: there the stop produced release, advocacy intervention, an apology and compensation. Here the analogous incident is an unregulated, recurring airport practice with no documented remedy, and it coexists with record-high 2025 violence.

Lower than Meridia: there border officers are trained, respectful, detention brief, with counsel, written reasons and compensation. Here the main port of entry has no trans regulations, demands surgery, and detains — a systematic rather than incidental gap.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime pairs an unusually protective legal-institutional core — decriminalisation, hate-crime enhancement, service and employment protections, repeated court victories for LGBT people, documented mass public acceptance — with two unremedied traveller-facing exposures. First, the main airport's absence of trans-interaction rules produced documented humiliating screening and detainment demanding surgery, a near-universal entry exposure with no shown remedy. Second, 2025 data records rising, organised anti-LGBT violence in which trans people bear the brunt, alongside dated lethal attacks on visible community events. Custody, if reached, defaults to birth-sex segregation, and its judicial remedy is unproven for foreign visitors. Protections keep this far above criminalising or exclusionary regimes; the border gap and patterned violence keep it below the well-remedied 0.65-0.75 band.
